parser.resume_recovered_from: the session rollout task boundary: a run that inherits an earlier transcript appends a task to an existing rollout, a fresh run opens one
parser.session_join: run dirs are grouped by the thread_id in the first stream record; the rollout filename carries the same session id
parser.run_to_task: each run id is matched to the unclaimed task_started whose started_at is nearest the run id timestamp (tolerance 900 s)
parser.first_request_input: the first token_count last_token_usage.input_tokens after the run task_started
parser.cumulative_input: the sum of last_token_usage.input_tokens over the run task

argv_note: No codex run carries a resume token in its recorded argv. The dialect appends "resume <session id>" to a codex exec argv, but argv is durably recorded only on the ephemeral live pointers and none of the codex pointers carries the token, so the resume is recovered from the rollout, the only durable record of the append. A pointer session_resumed flag is not a substitute: a pointer can carry the flag with no resume token in argv and a rollout that opened fresh, so the flag alone would report an inheritance that did not happen.
